title: Nanolith - A look at the prototype of this cyberpunk adventure game
body:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=o_FRQ02nigQ

Daniel (@dungeondive) previews a prototype of Nanolith, taking no payment and noting he rarely does crowdfunding coverage unless there's something worth showing. His first reason for wanting this one to exist is simple: there are far too few cyberpunk adventure games.

That prompts a genuine detour through his cyberpunk shelf — Bester's The Stars My Destination as ground zero, Rudy Rucker, Richard Paul Russo, Bruce Bethke who coined the word, Gibson's Sprawl trilogy — before landing on his favourite, John Shirley's City Come A-Walkin', from which he reads a passage on a punk band at length because it gets the punk rather than the cyber.

Mechanically, the standout is the stress system. Roll five action dice and assign them; every one rolled costs stress, and the stress track shrinks each time it triggers, so pushing your cybernetic body harder makes it fail sooner — theme and mechanism married. He also flags nano-sync abilities that let one hero spend a die to boost another's, and the hacker's sidekick bot, which downloads enemy programs and turns them back on their owners.

The encounter book and storybook interlock, with hidden information on the pages themselves. Concerns are Kickstarter-shaped: he hopes it avoids bloat, in a genre he notes is defined by being short and direct.

----

Which cyberpunk novel should more board games be stealing from?
